summary: Conditional DNS forwarder returns mixed A/CNAME causing control-plane mTLS ALPN negotiation failures for VPCE-connected private deployment
description:
Issue summary:
Customer on a Private deployment using VPCE to route control-plane traffic reports intermittent control-plane auth failures and gRPC stream ALPN negotiation errors. Symptoms appear correlated with DNS responses that sometimes resolve the control-plane hostname to a private address and sometimes to a VPCE alias CNAME that points to our regional gateway. Impact:
- Control-plane authentication (mTLS) fails intermittently for serving nodes behind the customer's egress proxy.
- Long-lived gRPC streams drop during model warmup and leading to degraded latency and increased retries.
Environment:
- Private deployment (customer-managed VPC) connected via VPC Endpoint (vpce-0a1b2c) to redwood control-plane in us-east-1.
- Customer uses an on-prem conditional DNS forwarder that returns mixed records depending on requester IP.
- Serving nodes run rwd-inference-agent v2.13.2.
Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) From serving node in customer's subnet, perform `dig +short control-api.redwood.internal` multiple times.
2) Observe alternating answers: sometimes a private 10.100.x.x A record; other times a CNAME -> control-api-east.redwood-hosting.com followed by public A records.
3) Start model streaming workload; gRPC connection produces ALPN error and TLS handshake aborted messages in agent logs.
Logs / errors captured:
- agent: "tls: handshake failure: no application protocol"
- agent: "mTLS: peer certificate subjectAltName mismatch (expected control-api.redwood.internal)"
- control-plane: "connection rejected: client cert present but CN doesn't match source IP route"
- dig traces: show varying TTLs and mixed RRsets for same query within seconds.
Customer notes:
- Conditional forwarder maps internal DC ranges to private A records, other sources to VPCE alias CNAMEs.
- This behavior started after customer's internal DNS team rolled out a forwarder update last week.
steps_taken: Requested pcap from customer during failure window
Validated alternating DNS answers via repeated dig from customer node
Reproduced name resolution variance from a test VM in the same peered VPC
Checked control-plane cert SANs and validated they expect control-api.redwood.internal and control-api-east.redwood-hosting.com as acceptable names
investigation_notes: 03/10 - Initial triage: DNS answers vary based on source IP seen by customer's resolver. Hypothesis: split-horizon/conditional forwarder returning different RR types causing mismatched SNI/SAN expectations.

03/11 - Confirmed VPCE alias CNAME path causes client to present SNI 'control-api-east.redwood-hosting.com' while agent's configured expected CN is 'control-api.redwood.internal' leading to SAN mismatch.

03/11 - Observed ALPN negotiation failures when the agent attempted HTTP/2 over TLS but received backend expecting a different SNI; some proxies re-wrote ALPN, producing 'no application protocol' error.
03/12 - Correlated spikes in gRPC disconnects with times when DNS TTL for the private A record expires and client re-resolves; suggests cached mixed answers across renewing nodes.
workaround: Advise customer to pin control-plane hostname in their local DNS by returning a consistent A record (private address) for the serving-subnet resolver; alternatively, add a conditional response that always returns the VPCE alias and ensure agent SNI configuration accepts the alias. Temporary option: set agent env var RWD_CONTROL_API_HOST_OVERRIDE to the static private IP to avoid resolution variance.
resolution_notes: Pending: engineering has a two-track plan. Short term, coordinate with customer's DNS team to deliver a consistent A record for control-api.redwood.internal to the serving node resolver (customer applied this change 2026-03-12 and reported reduced incidents). Long term, platform team will add SNI/CN acceptance mapping for VPCE alias CNAMEs and enhance agent to allow explicit control-plane host override and better ALPN fallback logging. A follow-up PR created: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/5421.
action_items: Support to confirm customer applied DNS pinning and monitor for 48h
Platform to add SNI accept-list for VPCE alias names (owner: eng-infra)
Engineering to add agent env var docs and a short-lived setting for private deployments (owner: dx)
comments: Maya Chen (Support) 2026-03-10: Customer reports ~10% of control-plane connects failing over past 36h. Provided dig output and agent logs.

Liam O'Connor (SRE) 2026-03-11: Reproduced mixed RR behavior from test VM. Suspect conditional forwarder; requesting customer's DNS team to map control-api redwood name consistently to avoid SNI flip.
Customer DNS (K. Alvarez) 2026-03-11: Confirmed we rolled out conditional forwarder last week. We can pin responses for the serving-subnet. ETA for change: 2026-03-12 03:00 UTC.

Liam O'Connor (SRE) 2026-03-12: Change applied by customer. Agent-side metrics show control-plane reconnects dropped to near zero in the 6 hours since. Leaving in progress until 48h observation window completes.
Maya Chen (Support) 2026-03-12: Opened linked engineering ticket for SNI mapping and agent override docs. Will follow up with customer for post-change verification)
